stem: Omeprazole is used alone or with other medications to treat the symptoms of which digestive condition?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None — GERD symptoms are a listed omeprazole use.
options.explanation: Omeprazole treats the symptoms of GERD, in which backward flow of stomach acid causes heartburn and possible injury to the esophagus.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Confuses acid-driven esophageal injury with immune-mediated colonic inflammation.
options.explanation: Ulcerative colitis is immune-mediated inflammation of the colonic mucosa, treated with aminosalicylates or immunosuppressants; acid suppression does not treat it.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Assumes any chronic gut symptom complex responds to acid suppression.
options.explanation: Irritable bowel syndrome is a functional bowel disorder managed with diet, antispasmodics or antidiarrheals; reducing stomach acid does not treat it.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Mistakes gluten-driven small-bowel injury for an acid-related disease.
options.explanation: Celiac disease is immune-mediated injury to the small-bowel mucosa triggered by gluten; the treatment is a strict gluten-free diet.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Blames every esophageal symptom on acid, missing achalasia's motility failure.
options.explanation: Achalasia is failure of the lower esophageal sphincter to relax after loss of inhibitory neurons; it is treated by dilation or myotomy, not acid suppression.

context: Learning objective: Omeprazole treats the symptoms of GERD, in which backward flow of stomach acid causes heartburn and possible esophageal injury.
